Apply this in the Zenodo browser UI: draft -> Edit -> fill the matching fields. See ZENODO_RELEASE.md. title: Raw fluorescence microscopy z-stacks for "Cellquant: a vibecoder's guide to image analysis"
description:
Raw, unprocessed multi-channel fluorescence microscopy image data underlying the figures and tables of Cellquant: a vibecoder's guide to image analysis. These are the source images for the analyses reproduced by the cellquant pipeline; no segmentation, projection, or quantification has been applied.

99 files, ~52.9 GB, in two datasets:

  • Tif6_Nsr1_Sis1_6hr/z-stacks/ — 86 three-channel yeast z-stacks. Saccharomyces cerevisiae after 6 h at one of five temperatures: 25 °C (16 fields), 30 °C (12), 32 °C (19), 36 °C (16) and 40 °C (23). Channels are Tif6, Nsr1 (nucleolar marker) and Sis1. These support the yeast temperature series, the colocalization and nucleolar-proximity analyses, and the dimensionality-reduction figures.
  • SG_zstacks/ — 6 three-channel HCT116 z-stacks (3 control, 3 sodium arsenite), plus SG_zstacks/MIPs/ containing 7 maximum-intensity projections (4 arsenite, 3 control). Channels are DAPI, G3BP1 and PABPC1. These support the mammalian stress-granule analyses.

Files are TIFF. Voxel size is carried in the image metadata and is read directly by the analysis pipeline; in three dimensions cellquant refuses to run without it rather than assume isotropic 1 µm voxels.

Reproducing the analysis. The analysis code is a single Python script, cellquant.py, archived separately and developed at github.com/davidpincus/cellquant. Cropped example subsets ship inside that repository, so the tutorials can be run without downloading this 52.9 GB archive; download this deposit only to reproduce the published figures from the original data. The validation_3d/ directory of the repository contains the harness that regenerates the manuscript figures and tables from these images.
